description.narrative:
Den 23 maj 2018 inkom UNDP med ansökan om finansiering av ett miljöprogram, "UNDP Towards Environmental Sustainability in Cambodia". En reviderad version av ansökan inlämnades den 10 juli 2018. Programmet kommer att genomföras under perioden 2018-2020.
Syftet med insatsen är att bistå Kambodja i att nå de globala utvecklingsmålen, mer specifikt mål 15: "skydda, återställa och främja ett hållbart nyttjande av landbaserade ekosystem, hålllbart bruka skogar, bekämpa ökenspridning, hejda och vrida tillbaka markförstöringen samt hejda förlusten av biologisk mångfald; mål 12: säkerställa hållbara konsumptions- och produktionsmönster; samt mål 7: säkerställa tillgången till en ekonomiskt överkomlig, tillförlitlig, hållbar och modern energi för alla.
Programmet avser främja miljömässigt hållbara modeller i riktade områden i samverkan med myndigheter, civilsamhälle samt genom publika/privata partnerskap. Genom programmet eftersträvas följande mål: 1) flera områden under hållbar naturvårdsskötsel 2) minskat, återanvänt avfall genom cirkulära ekonomiska modeller 3) bättrad tillgång till ren, ekonomisk tillgänglig, och hållbar energi för fattig landsbygdsbefolkning 4) utvecklande av miljöfrämjande policies och stärkt policykoordinering.
Insatsens totala belopp uppgår till 49,1 MSEK, utav vilket Sida ombeds bidra med 16 500 000 SEK.

The objective of the intervention is to enable Cambodia to attain the Sustainable Development Goals, more specifically goal 15: life on land; goal 12: responsible consumption and production, and goal 7: affordable and clean energy. The programme aims to design and implement innovative environmentally sustainable models in specifically targeted areas through public and private partnerships. The programme will attain the following four outputs: -more areas placed under sustainable management -waste reduced, recycled and reused through application of circular economy models -improved access to clean, affordable, and sustainable energy for the rural poor -enabling policies developed and policy coordination enhanced.

The programme was designed to develop innovative responses to address a number of environmental problems that Cambodia is facing due to its rapid economic growth and development. The issues were selected based on impact and severity of the problems but also on interest and ownership from the Government of Cambodia as well as the private sectors, as public private partnership were promoted models across each of the thematic outputs. The problems to be addressed were: 1) degradation of natural resources; 2) growing volume of waste; and 3) limited access to affordable, sustainable, and clean energy among the poor. More specifically, the three following outputs are:
Output 1: Community Based Natural Resource Management (CBNRM) institutions strengthened and financial resources mobilized for sustainable Nature Resourece Management (NRM)
Output 2: Waste reduced, recycled and reused through application of circular economy models
Output 3: Improved access to clean, affordable, and sustainable energy for the rural poor

The work related to the three different outputs were structured in similar manners with pilot projects at the field level to showcase and demonstrate viability in parallel with policy development to overcome structural challenges as well as to raise awareness and gain tracking for scaling up of initiatives. This model of addressing challenges lends itself to specific problems with proven technical solution that need to be adopted to the local context and gain acceptance from regulators and policy owners.
Under output 1 that relates to the degradation of natural resources, one of the main challenge has been that the financial and human resources allocated for the management of the large areas of protected lands is inadequate - 41% of Cambodia has been designated as protected land but the government budget is minimal and the area is managed by only 1,260 rangers. The project promoted the concept of Payment for Ecosystem Services (PES) where funds are raised through partnerships with the private sector and companies that are willing to pay for specific services that are important for their business model - for example tourist companies that are willing to pay for conservation of natural habitats that attract tourists or beverage companies that agree to fund watershed management that will secure a sustainable supply of high quality ground water. Under the Building an Enabling Environment for Sustainable Developmnet (BESD) project this relatively novel concept was introduced to Cambodia and a National Road Map for Payment of Ecosystem services that defines the overall vision and identifies priority actions for scaling up pilot initiatives to the national level. To promote awareness of the PES concept, a national dialogue was initiated that brought together 160 participants from government, academia, civil society and private sector. In parallel with the policy development and dialogue, two PES pilots were initiated that focused on the impact of deforestation in Kulen Mountain on the water supply to down stream Siem Reap as well as the willingness to pay study of the tourism and hospitality industry. The results under this output has defined PES strategy for Cambodia and paved the way for full operationalization of the two PES pilots that is planned to take place under UNDP's bio financing initiative and the Cambodia Sustainable Landscape Initiative. As a response to impact of the the Covid pandemic, additional resources were allocated under output 1 to allow for the implementation of a cash for work scheme targeting reforestation of degraded forest lands. This cash for work component benefited 2810 people form 1915 vulnerable families from the most affected provinces and replanted a total of 182 Ha with indigenous tree seedlings.
The output 2 targeting Circular Economy (CE) produced several policy oriented results. A major results was the development and approval of the National Circular Economy Strategy and Action Plan 2021-2035. The CE strategy defined closing the loop of the entire value chain (production, distribution, consumption, waste generation, and waste treatment) as a national goal. The plan also outlined a clear roadmap, along with short-, medium-, and long-term priority actions to enable Cambodias transition to a circular economy. The roles of different ministries, private sector, development partners, academic and civil societies were clearly defined for the proposed actions. Another key achievement was the drafting of a sub-decree on plastic management - plastic waste having become a increasingly visible problem given the economic and population growth. Under this component and in collaboration with H&M, a joint assessment was done to explore the waste to energy in the garment in order to limit the negative environmental impact. This resulted in the development of guidelines and manuals as well as recommendations aimed at regulators for minimizing public hazard. In partnership with Kep Municipality, circular economy aspects was integrated into its five year development plan and municipal level pricing was established for the solid waste management. The project also supported the establishment of a unit for municipal waste management at Kep Municipality. Cambodia's favourable conditions for solar energy are not adequately exploited due to an unfavorable regulatory and policy environment mainly due to "dominant, powerful interest in support for coal based energy".
For output 3, a number of high quality and insightful reports have been prepared related to the benefits of solar power. The studies have been led by the Ministry of Environment in consultation with other relevant ministries but final product has not in all cases been approved by the Ministry of Mines and Energy. This further illustrates that most of the challenges related to solar energy are political rather than financial or technical. The project also piloted interventions in energy efficiency in the building sector - of the sectors with the largest energy demand in Cambodia. This resulted in the development of the Energy Efficiency Design Guidelines for Residential and Commercial Buildings. Output 3 also focused on hard to reach off-grid communities with the construction of two mini-grids serving 225 vulnerable households (approximately 1,250 people) in three villages in Kampong Chhang province. The mini-grids also included street lighting increasing security after dark especially for women and children.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
